title: test(settle): raise integration coverage of the settler above 60 percent
description: The settler has the lowest measured coverage in the repository. Bring its Postgres-backed paths under test: exposure calculation, the four sweep triggers, submission intent and restart reconciliation, retry escalation, and the metrics queries.
why: `go test ./internal/... -cover` reports **8.4% for internal/settle**, the lowest of any package, against 1248 lines of source. Much of the gap is that its tests need Postgres and skip without it, but that means the money path is effectively unexercised on any machine without Docker, and coverage in CI is the only place it is ever measured. A regression in Decide, Submit or ReconcileSubmitting would not be caught locally by anyone.
criteria: `go test ./internal/settle/ -cover` reports at least 60% with Postgres available
Each of §6's four sweep triggers has a test, plus the wait case and the never-settle-at-or-below-last-settled rule

internal/settle/policy.go's Decide is a pure function and needs no database; the cheapest coverage is there first.

title: refactor(workspace): stop discarding errors from deferred Close calls
description: Twelve deferred Close calls drop their error. Capture and log each, or document per site why the error genuinely cannot matter.
why: CLAUDE.md §8 is unambiguous: "Never discard an error, not even in a defer — log it." There are **12** `defer x.Close()` sites in non-test code, including internal/stellar/rpc.go:96, internal/pricebook/fetch.go:70, internal/settle/metrics.go:135 and internal/settle/daemon.go:101. On an HTTP response body a dropped Close error is usually benign; on a pgx rows handle it can mask a connection the pool then reuses, which in the settler's metrics and daemon queries is the money path.
criteria: No non-test `defer x.Close()` discards its error without an accompanying comment saying why
pgx rows.Close sites log at WARN with the query context when Close reports an error
A grep-based test or CI step asserts the pattern cannot return
go vet and staticcheck stay clean
guidance: internal/settle/metrics.go:135 and daemon.go:101 are the two that matter most; an HTTP body Close is the benign end of the range.
The idiom is a named return plus `defer func(){ if err := c.Close(); err != nil {...} }()` — keep it readable rather than mechanical.
Where the error genuinely cannot matter, a one-line comment saying so satisfies §8 better than silently dropping it.
